blogs.title: Patches Over Tokens: How Dynamic Compute Allocation is Reshaping LLM Architecture
blogs.description: An exploration of the fundamental shift from fixed tokenization to dynamic 'patching.' This post explains how the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) allocates computational resources based on data complexity rather than a static dictionary, significantly improving efficiency in unpredictable inputs.

blogs.title: Why Raw Bytes Might Be Smarter Than Subwords: The Case for Byte-Large Language Models
blogs.description: Discovering the hidden advantages of training on raw bytes. We explain how bypassing heuristics like byte-pair encoding (BPE) leads to superior robustness against noisy inputs, better character-level understanding (orthography), and improved performance in low-resource languages.

blogs.title: The New Scaling Law: Doubling Model Size Without Increasing Inference Cost
blogs.description: Breaking the floor on LLM efficiency. Learn how BLT allows developers to simultaneously increase both model parameters and patch size while maintaining a fixed inference budget, unlocking new performance tiers that were previously unattainable with token-based architectures.
